s1.d: Chrono tells you in one sentence if something is wrong. This tour plays by itself: move on at your own pace with Next or the arrow keys, and leave any time with Esc.

s2.d: Muted green: all good. Amber: slow. Red: not responding. Click one and the list takes you to that service.

s3.d: Services with problems move up to the "Need attention" group and say what is happening and since when. Healthy ones stay below, quiet.

s4.d: You get min, average, max and p95, plus the last 24 hours as a curve. Move the cursor over the chart to read each moment.

s5.d: The actions show up when you hover a row. Pin the services you care about most to keep them at hand.

s6.d: Keep only what has problems, or only your pinned services. The number on each filter tells you how many there are.

s7.d: Each bar is 30 minutes of your whole fleet and takes the worst state of that moment. The big number is the share of time it was operational.

s8.d: Here you see what is happening now and the latest ones. For the full history, open "View all incidents".

s9.t: What is happening now, on top
s9.d: The ongoing incident is featured, with its curve and a live elapsed time. If there is none, it shows the latest one. Next to it, the summary: how many incidents, how much time they affected and how long they last.

s10.t: Filter by service, type and period
s10.d: Combine the filters to find exactly what you need, for example only outages from the last 24 hours.

s11.d: You see when it started and ended, how long it lasted and, if it happened in the last 24 hours, the latency curve with that moment marked.

s12.d: Watch what happens if OpenAI stops responding: the headline changes, the logo "o" turns red, a badge appears on Incidents and the service moves up to the attention group.

s13.d: Type a name and its address. It shows up right away as "Waiting for data" and fills in with the first check.

s14.d: Switch between light and dark, and between Spanish and English, whenever you like.

s15.d: You know the essentials. You can watch this tutorial again from the button at the top, or trigger an outage yourself.
